Judicial.label: Judicial Branch
Judicial.blurb: Interprets laws and ensures they comply with the Constitution.

Executive.label: Executive Branch
Executive.blurb: Enforces laws and administers federal programs.

Military.label: Military / Defense
Military.blurb: Protects national security under civilian control.

education.title: Federal Appellate Courts
education.description: The US is divided into 12 regional circuits (11 numbered plus the DC Circuit). A 13th, the Federal Circuit, has nationwide jurisdiction over specialized cases and is not shown on the map.
education.purpose: Review decisions from district courts and ensure consistent application of federal law across the country.
education.whyItMatters: Circuit courts create binding precedents that affect millions of people. Conflicts between circuits often lead to Supreme Court review.

education.title: Federal Bankruptcy System
education.description: Specialized federal courts handling bankruptcy cases. There are 90 bankruptcy courts, organized within the 94 federal judicial districts. This map currently groups them at the circuit level; district-level boundaries are planned.
education.purpose: Provide relief to debtors and fair distribution to creditors under federal bankruptcy law.
education.whyItMatters: Hundreds of thousands of bankruptcy cases are filed annually, affecting individuals, families, and businesses nationwide.

education.title: Federal Emergency Management
education.description: FEMA divides the US into 10 regions to coordinate disaster response and emergency management.
education.purpose: Coordinate federal disaster response, provide aid to states during emergencies, and support disaster preparedness.
education.whyItMatters: FEMA responds to hurricanes, floods, wildfires, and other disasters affecting millions of Americans annually.

education.title: Environmental Protection
education.description: The EPA uses 10 regions to enforce environmental laws and regulations. This 10-region layout is the federal government's standard regional system, shared by many agencies.
education.purpose: Protect human health and the environment by enforcing regulations on air, water, and land quality.
education.whyItMatters: The EPA sets standards for clean air and water that affect every American, and enforces laws like the Clean Air Act.

education.title: America's Central Bank
education.description: The Federal Reserve System divides the US into 12 districts, each served by a regional Federal Reserve Bank. The Fed is an independent central bank — it operates within the government but its monetary policy decisions do not require approval by the President or Congress.
education.purpose: Conduct monetary policy, supervise banks, maintain financial stability, and provide payment services.
education.whyItMatters: The Fed's decisions on interest rates ripple through the entire economy, from mortgage rates to job markets. District boundaries still reflect the economic geography of 1913.

education.title: National Demographics
education.description: The Census Bureau divides the US into 4 major regions: Northeast, Midwest, South, and West.
education.purpose: Organize demographic data collection and analysis for the constitutionally mandated census.
education.whyItMatters: Census data determines congressional representation, electoral votes, and how roughly $1.5 trillion in federal funds is distributed each year.

education.title: Regional Demographics
education.description: 9 divisions nested within the 4 census regions: New England, Middle Atlantic, East/West North Central, South Atlantic, East/West South Central, Mountain, and Pacific.
education.purpose: Provide more detailed regional analysis of population, economy, and social characteristics.
education.whyItMatters: Division-level data helps track regional economic and demographic trends across America.

education.title: Federal Education Administration
education.description: The Department of Education uses the standard federal 10-region system (the same layout as EPA and FEMA) to administer its programs.
education.purpose: Distribute federal education funding, enforce civil rights in schools, and collect education data.
education.whyItMatters: The department manages tens of billions of dollars in K-12 funding and the federal student loan programs affecting millions of students.

education.title: Public Lands Management
education.description: The Bureau of Land Management manages about 245 million acres of public land — roughly 1/10 of the US — through a hierarchy of 12 state offices and about 200 district and field offices, mostly in western states.
education.purpose: Manage public lands for multiple uses: energy development, grazing, recreation, and conservation.
education.established: 1946 (merger of Grazing Service and General Land Office)
education.whyItMatters: BLM manages more land than any other federal agency, balancing economic use with conservation.

education.title: Maritime Defense & Safety
education.description: 9 Coast Guard districts cover US coastlines, the Great Lakes, and inland waterways. In peacetime the Coast Guard operates under DHS rather than the Department of Defense.
education.purpose: Maritime law enforcement, search and rescue, environmental protection, and coastal security.
education.established: 1915 (merger of Revenue Cutter Service and Life-Saving Service)
education.whyItMatters: The Coast Guard saves thousands of lives annually and enforces laws across 95,000 miles of coastline.
